cues.en: The embeddings, matrices, and vectors that we've been working with so far are tied to
cues.zh: 目前使用的嵌入矩陣與向量，都對應

cues.en: specific subwords, so tokens.
cues.zh: 特定子詞，也就是 token。

cues.en: But there is another matrix of embeddings in language models, and this is called the position embeddings.
cues.zh: 但語言模型裡，還有另一個嵌入矩陣，稱為位置嵌入。

cues.en: These have a different function compared to the token embeddings.
cues.zh: 它的功能，與 token 嵌入不同。

cues.en: They're also easier to visualize.
cues.zh: 也比較容易視覺化。

cues.en: Are they kind of easier to understand?
cues.zh: 那是否比較容易理解？

cues.en: Superficially, they seem easier to understand, but the devil's in the details.
cues.zh: 表面上似乎如此，但細節才是真正難的地方。

cues.en: Anyway, in this video, I'm going to motivate why we need position embeddings and then discuss what they look like and where they come from.
cues.zh: 這支影片，會說明為什麼需要位置嵌入，再談它的樣貌與來源。

cues.en: And the upshot is that position embeddings are kind of like temporal weighting functions
cues.zh: 重點是，位置嵌入有點像時間加權函式，

cues.en: that allow the model to stay focused on a token that was presented a few words ago, or a few sentences ago, or maybe even a few paragraphs ago.
cues.zh: 讓模型能持續關注幾個字、幾句，甚至幾段之前出現的 token。

cues.en: Here is an example of the type of problem that position embeddings allow language models to solve.
cues.zh: 這裡示範，位置嵌入能幫語言模型解決哪種問題。

cues.en: This is a couple of sentences that I got from the Wikipedia page on hazelnuts.
cues.zh: 這是 Wikipedia 榛果頁面上的幾個句子。

cues.en: So hazelnuts are used as a snack food in baking and desserts, and in breakfast cereals such as muesli, in confectionary they.
cues.zh: 榛果可作為零食，用於烘焙與甜點，以及什錦穀片等早餐穀物。在糖果製作中，它們……

cues.en: Okay, what does this word they refer to?
cues.zh: 這裡的「它們」指什麼？

cues.en: Now in theory, this word they could refer to any plural noun that is present in this
cues.zh: 理論上，可以指這個

cues.en: sentence like hazelnuts, food, desserts, cereals, or muesli, but that's not all.
cues.zh: 句子中的任何複數名詞，例如榛果、食物、甜點、穀物或什錦穀片，還不只如此。

cues.en: They could also refer to some other plural noun that appeared before this sentence.
cues.zh: 也可能指這個句子之前，出現的某個複數名詞。

cues.en: For example, people who work in a hazelnut factory or in a bakery.
cues.zh: 例如，在榛果工廠或麵包店工作的人。

cues.en: Now you know from context that the word they almost certainly refers to hazelnuts, but
cues.zh: 你從上下文知道，「它們」幾乎確定是指榛果，

cues.en: a language model doesn't know that sort of thing a priori.
cues.zh: 但語言模型事先並不知道這類事情。

cues.en: So we need a way to allow the language model to hold on to the activations.
cues.zh: 所以，需要方法，讓語言模型保留活化。

cues.en: It's like keeping a trace of the token embeddings active for important tokens that happen before
cues.zh: 就像為這個字之前的重要 token，保留

cues.en: this word here, and you don't want to just hold on to all of the tokens because most
cues.zh: token 嵌入的活躍痕跡。但不想保留全部 token，因為大多數

cues.en: of these tokens are not relevant for understanding what they refers to, and we also don't necessarily
cues.zh: 與理解「它們」的指涉無關；也不一定

cues.en: want some kind of like linear decay just going back in time because it's not the case that confectionary is the most important word for interpreting the word they.
cues.zh: 想要單純隨時間往前線性衰減，因為 confectionary 並不是理解「它們」最重要的字。

cues.en: In fact, the model should be able to key in on words like hazelnuts and cereals while
cues.zh: 模型應該能抓住榛果、穀物之類的字，

cues.en: also realizing that certain words in the past like in or as or commas are not going to be
cues.zh: 也知道先前某些字，例如 in、as 或逗號，

cues.en: relevant for figuring out what they refers to and therefore what the next token should be.
cues.zh: 對理解「它們」指什麼，以及下一個 token 該是什麼，並不重要。

cues.en: So this is the problem that position embeddings help LLMs solve.
cues.zh: 這就是位置嵌入，協助 LLM 解決的問題。

cues.en: So here's a little bit more detail.
cues.zh: 再詳細一點。

cues.en: LLMs have no built-in way to represent time or positions between tokens.
cues.zh: LLM 沒有內建方式，表示 token 之間的時間或位置。

cues.en: And by ordinal distances here, I mean that any pair of tokens could be separated by somewhere
cues.zh: 這裡的順序距離，是指任意兩個 token，中間可能隔著

cues.en: between zero other tokens and a thousand other tokens.
cues.zh: 0 到 1,000 個其他 token。

cues.en: Unfortunately, modern LLMs have context windows of many tens of thousands of tokens.
cues.zh: 不過，現代 LLM 的上下文視窗，可達數萬個 token。

cues.en: GPT-2 can only take a thousand twenty four tokens at a time.
cues.zh: GPT-2 一次只能接受 1,024 個。

cues.en: But anyway, the LLMs don't have a way of representing something like, for example, two tokens that are separated by 13 other tokens.
cues.zh: 總之，LLM 本身沒有方法表示，例如，中間隔著 13 個 token 的兩個 token，

cues.en: And yet these two tokens are still related to each other.
cues.zh: 卻仍然彼此相關。

cues.en: So the positions vectors allow the models to increase or decrease the embeddings for tokens depending on their ordinal position.
cues.zh: 位置向量，讓模型能依 token 的順序位置，提高或降低嵌入值。

cues.en: OK, so where do these position embeddings come from and what do they look like?
cues.zh: 這些位置嵌入，從哪裡來？又長什麼樣？

cues.en: Well, let me answer that first question first.
cues.zh: 先回答第一個問題。

cues.en: Just like with token embeddings, position embeddings can be trained through gradient
cues.zh: 和 token 嵌入一樣，位置嵌入可以根據資料，透過梯度

cues.en: descent based on data or they can be predefined based on some mathematical properties.
cues.zh: 下降訓練，也可以依某些數學性質預先定義。

cues.en: This is also sometimes called fixed.
cues.zh: 後者有時也叫固定式。

cues.en: So trained position embeddings are initialized as random numbers and then optimized with training data and the gradient descent algorithm.
cues.zh: 可訓練的位置嵌入，先初始化成隨機數，再用訓練資料與梯度下降最佳化。

cues.en: This is good because then the position embeddings are optimized for performance on the data that the model is trained on.
cues.zh: 好處是，位置嵌入能針對模型訓練資料上的表現，進行最佳化。

cues.en: But it does mean that we have some additional parameters to train.
cues.zh: 但也代表，多一些參數要訓練。

cues.en: But you know, language models have so many parameters to train that an extra few thousand here there is not really a big deal in the grand scheme of things.
cues.zh: 不過，語言模型本來就有那麼多參數，整體而言，多幾千個其實不算什麼。

cues.en: Alternatively, position embeddings can be defined from mathematical formulas that have certain desired characteristics.
cues.zh: 另一種方式，是用具有所需特性的數學公式，定義位置嵌入。

cues.en: They often come from sine and cosine to capture temporal sequences, kind of like the Fourier transform.
cues.zh: 常使用正弦與餘弦捕捉時間序列，有點像傅立葉轉換。

cues.en: I'll show you the formulas and the code for this in a few moments.
cues.zh: 稍後展示公式與程式。

cues.en: But an advantage here is that you don't need any additional training to get these position vectors to work.
cues.zh: 優點是，不需要額外訓練，就能使用這些位置向量。

cues.en: But on the other hand, the combinations of sinusoidal position embeddings can become really complicated for real world language data.
cues.zh: 但另一方面，對真實語言資料，正弦式位置嵌入的組合，可能變得非常複雜。

cues.en: If you are familiar with signal processing or Fourier analysis, you might think about
cues.zh: 如果熟悉訊號處理或傅立葉分析，可以類比

cues.en: an analogy with using the Fourier transform to represent a square or an edge or some other non sinusoidal feature.
cues.zh: 用傅立葉轉換表示方波、邊緣，或其他非正弦特徵。

cues.en: If you're not familiar with the Fourier transform, then don't worry about the analogy.
cues.zh: 如果不熟傅立葉轉換，不必擔心這個比喻，

cues.en: It's not that important.
cues.zh: 並不重要。

cues.en: Here again is this attention is all you need paper.
cues.zh: 又是這篇 Attention Is All You Need。

cues.en: This paper was quite influential in the history of LLMs.
cues.zh: 它在 LLM 歷史上影響很大，

cues.en: So you'll see it pretty often when learning about language models.
cues.zh: 學語言模型時，會經常看到。

cues.en: Now a few videos ago, I showed you a screenshot of their section on embeddings and unembeddings.
cues.zh: 幾支影片前，展示過其中嵌入與反嵌入章節的截圖。

cues.en: Here is some text from a different part of the paper about position embeddings.
cues.zh: 這是論文另一部分，談位置嵌入。

cues.en: The key point is that they used predefined embeddings and those are based on sine and
cues.zh: 關鍵是，他們使用預先定義的嵌入，以 token

cues.en: cosine of the ordinal position of the tokens.
cues.zh: 順序位置的正弦與餘弦為基礎。

cues.en: Here are some other texts that's a little bit later where they say that they also tried learned or trained position embeddings and they produced very similar results.
cues.zh: 後面另一段說，也試過學習、訓練出的位置嵌入，結果非常相似。

cues.en: So they chose the predefined or mathematically defined position embeddings because whatever reasons they say here, honestly, this sounds a bit speculative to me.
cues.zh: 所以，選擇預先、以數學定義的位置嵌入，原因寫在這裡；老實說，我覺得有點推測性。

cues.en: Anyway, in modern commercially available larger models, it's more common to train the position
cues.zh: 總之，現代商用大型模型，比較常從資料訓練位置

cues.en: embeddings from data than to predefine them for basically these reasons that I outlined here.
cues.zh: 嵌入，而不是預先定義，大致基於這裡列出的理由。

cues.en: In a moment, I'm going to switch to Python, but first I want to give you a heads up of what we're going to do and what to look for.
cues.zh: 稍後切換到 Python，先提醒會做什麼、該看什麼。

cues.en: So we will import the GPT-2 model and extract the position embeddings matrix.
cues.zh: 匯入 GPT-2 模型，擷取位置嵌入矩陣。

cues.en: We will visualize some random vectors that might look something like this.
cues.zh: 隨機畫出一些向量，可能像這樣。

cues.en: Now these are pretty interesting to look at.
cues.zh: 很有意思。

cues.en: So the x-axis here is the ordinal position of the tokens with zero on the left side corresponding
cues.zh: x 軸是 token 的順序位置，左側 0 對應

cues.en: to the start of the text that you input into the GPT model.
cues.zh: 輸入 GPT 模型文字的開頭。

cues.en: And as we go to the right, that corresponds to the end of the context window, which is how many tokens a model can process in a sequence.
cues.zh: 往右，對應上下文視窗的結尾，也就是模型一次能處理的序列長度。

cues.en: Then in GPT-2, the context window is 1024 tokens.
cues.zh: GPT-2 的上下文視窗，是 1,024 個 token。

cues.en: GPT-4 models have varying context window sizes depending on the model architecture, but it's in the range of 10,000 to 100,000.
cues.zh: GPT-4 視窗大小依模型架構不同，大約在一萬到十萬個 token。

cues.en: So what do these wiggly lines actually mean?
cues.zh: 這些彎曲的線，究竟代表什麼？

cues.en: So these correspond to the weightings on the token embeddings relative to each other.
cues.zh: 它們對應 token 嵌入彼此相對的加權。

cues.en: So how do we interpret these wobbly things?
cues.zh: 怎麼解讀這些起伏？

cues.en: Let's imagine that we entered a text that is 1024 tokens long.
cues.zh: 假設輸入一段長 1,024 個 token 的文字，

cues.en: Maybe that text corresponds to a few paragraphs.
cues.zh: 也許是幾個段落。

cues.en: Here towards the left is the very beginning of the text and here to the right is the very end of the text.
cues.zh: 左側是文字開頭，右側是文字結尾。

cues.en: So if we focus for a moment on this one here, which happens to be vector 402, we see that
cues.zh: 先看這個，剛好是第 402 個向量，可以看到，

cues.en: this model is going to have a strong positive weight on recent tokens and a negative weight on the tokens towards the beginning of the text.
cues.zh: 模型對近期 token 有很強的正權重，對文字前段的 token 則有負權重。

cues.en: So this dimension, this vector, will contribute to basically like a linear decrease of importance
cues.zh: 所以，這個維度、這個向量，會讓越早出現的文字，

cues.en: or focus going further back in the text as we go along.
cues.zh: 重要程度或關注程度，大致線性降低。

cues.en: Although there's also a strong peak at the beginning.
cues.zh: 但最開頭，也有個很強的峰值。

cues.en: So this positions vector would facilitate the model linking something that was mentioned at the very beginning of the text to, for example, a summary that happened at the end
cues.zh: 因此，這個位置向量，有助於模型把文字最開頭提到的內容，連到

cues.en: of the token sequence.
cues.zh: token 序列末尾的摘要。

cues.en: And this one down here is also pretty interesting.
cues.zh: 下方這個也很有意思，

cues.en: This has a big peak at the center.
cues.zh: 中間有個大峰值。

cues.en: So this would facilitate the model highlighting tokens that appear in the middle of the text, but not so much in the beginning or the end of the text.
cues.zh: 有助於強調文字中間出現的 token，而不是開頭或結尾。

cues.en: I'm tempted to use the word attention here that these vectors are helping the model attend to tokens happening at various ordinal positions throughout the text.
cues.zh: 很想用「注意」這個詞，說這些向量幫模型關注文字各順序位置的 token。

cues.en: The problem is that the word attention means a very specific thing in the context of large language models and transformers.
cues.zh: 但問題是，attention 在 LLM 與 Transformer 情境中，有非常特定的意義。

cues.en: So I'm reluctant to use the word attention here, but I think you know what I mean.
cues.zh: 所以，不太想在這裡用它，不過你應該懂意思。

cues.en: And what do these numerical values actually mean?
cues.zh: 這些數值，究竟代表什麼？

cues.en: Well, zero is inherently interpretable because it means that the vector is not providing any particular weight for that token position.
cues.zh: 0 本身容易解讀，表示向量沒有對該 token 位置提供特定權重。

cues.en: So that you see here, for example.
cues.zh: 例如，這裡。

cues.en: However, the positive and negative values are not so easily interpreted.
cues.zh: 但正值與負值，就沒那麼容易解讀。

cues.en: They do not necessarily correspond to increasing versus decreasing the activation in the model,
cues.zh: 不一定對應模型活化的增加或降低，

cues.en: nor do they necessarily trivially correspond to increasing or decreasing the probability of selecting a particular token.
cues.zh: 也不一定直接對應選取某個 token 的機率增減。

cues.en: The thing is that the impact of the signs on these position vectors depends on the correspondence
cues.zh: 位置向量正負號的影響，取決於 token 嵌入處理時，

cues.en: with the signs of the model weights as the token embeddings are processed.
cues.zh: 與模型權重正負號的對應關係。

cues.en: So it's all quite complicated and it defies a really simple, straightforward explanation.
cues.zh: 所以，很複雜，無法用非常簡單、直接的方式解釋。

cues.en: But it certainly is the case that these position vectors translate into the model being able
cues.zh: 但確實，這些位置向量，讓模型處理不同 token 時，

cues.en: to incorporate token position, ordinal position, as it is processing the different tokens.
cues.zh: 能納入 token 的順序位置。

cues.en: Now you will learn more about these position embedding vectors in the next video and also in a later section.
cues.zh: 下一支影片，以及後面章節，會更深入學習位置嵌入向量。

cues.en: But anyway, moving along.
cues.zh: 總之，繼續。

cues.en: The next plot we're going to look at will be matrices of cosine similarities within
cues.zh: 接著看餘弦相似度矩陣，分別比較

cues.en: each embedding vector over time and across the different position embedding vectors.
cues.zh: 各嵌入向量跨時間的關係，以及不同位置嵌入向量彼此的關係。

cues.en: Let me first focus your attention on this right side panel.
cues.zh: 先看右側圖。

cues.en: This is a 768 by 768 matrix.
cues.zh: 這是 768 乘以 768 矩陣。

cues.en: The value of each element in this matrix is the cosine similarity between every possible pair of position embeddings vectors.
cues.zh: 每個元素，是每一對位置嵌入維度向量之間的餘弦相似度。

cues.en: Now you don't really see a lot happening in this image.
cues.zh: 圖裡看不出太多變化。

cues.en: In fact, almost all of the cosine similarities are close to zero.
cues.zh: 其實，幾乎所有餘弦相似度都接近 0。

cues.en: Not exactly zero, but fairly close to zero.
cues.zh: 不完全是 0，但相當接近。

cues.en: You don't see a lot of structure happening in here.
cues.zh: 看不到很多結構。

cues.en: And what that means is that all of the position embedding vectors are fairly uncorrelated with each other.
cues.zh: 這表示，這些位置嵌入向量彼此相當不相關。

cues.en: In other words, each position embeddings vector makes an independent and unique contribution to decomposing the temporal sequence of tokens.
cues.zh: 換句話說，各向量對拆解 token 的時間序列，提供獨立、獨特的貢獻。

cues.en: And that is what allows for basically any possible combination of sequence weightings to be learned by the model.
cues.zh: 因此，模型基本上能學習任何序列加權組合。

cues.en: Now all of these vectors are not exactly orthogonal.
cues.zh: 這些向量並不是完全正交。

cues.en: In fact, there is some meaningful structure in here that we will explore in the next video.
cues.zh: 其實，有些有意義的結構，下一支影片會探索。

cues.en: Alright, so that's for the cosine similarity across the different embeddings vectors.
cues.zh: 這是不同嵌入向量之間的餘弦相似度，

cues.en: So this one and this one, this one and this one, and so on.
cues.zh: 例如這個與這個，這個與這個，等等。

cues.en: On the other hand, this one over here is much more colorful and interesting to look at.
cues.zh: 另一張，則色彩豐富得多，也更有趣。

cues.en: So here we have the cosine similarities over the token indices.
cues.zh: 這裡，是 token 位置索引之間的餘弦相似度。

cues.en: And this I find easier to think about as time.
cues.zh: 我比較容易把它想成時間。

cues.en: So if you think about the 1000 token positions as like time, because you're reading the text
cues.zh: 若把約 1,000 個 token 位置視為時間，因為閱讀文字

cues.en: over time, then these bands across the diagonal indicate the tendencies of the embeddings
cues.zh: 隨時間進行，那麼對角線旁的帶狀結構，就表示嵌入

cues.en: vectors to be correlated with their neighboring tokens and anti-correlated with tokens that are further away.
cues.zh: 在鄰近 token 位置傾向相關，而和較遠的位置反相關。

cues.en: You can see that as well when you look back at these specific examples.
cues.zh: 回頭看特定例子，也能看出。

cues.en: So each time point or token index position is strongly correlated with its neighbor.
cues.zh: 每個時間點，也就是 token 位置，與相鄰位置高度相關。

cues.en: And you see a lot of like almost rhythmic patterns.
cues.zh: 也有很多近似節奏的模式。

cues.en: So these position vectors tend to go up and down over the context window.
cues.zh: 這些位置向量，傾向在上下文視窗中上下起伏。

cues.en: And that's basically what this alternating pattern of yellow and blue indicates across the off diagonal.
cues.zh: 這就是非對角區域，黃藍交替模式的意思。

cues.en: Okay, the final thing we will look at in this code is the formula for predefining position
cues.zh: 最後，這段程式要看預先定義位置

cues.en: embeddings vectors as it was used in the attention paper that I showed the screenshot of in the previous slide.
cues.zh: 嵌入向量的公式，也就是前一張截圖的注意力論文使用的方法。

cues.en: So here the x-axis is token order also here, which again I like to think about as time.
cues.zh: 這裡與這裡的 x 軸，都是 token 順序；我同樣喜歡想成時間。

cues.en: And here the y-axis is the sorted embedding dimension.
cues.zh: y 軸是排序後的嵌入維度，

cues.en: And it's sorted by the frequency of the sine wave that's used to generate these vectors.
cues.zh: 依照產生向量的正弦波頻率排序。

cues.en: And these horizontal colored lines here correspond to the individual vectors that I have picked out for plotting over here.

cues.en: A couple of points of summary and conclusion.
cues.zh: 幾個總結與結論。

cues.en: The position embeddings vectors can decompose the token sequence into a set of independent temporal basis functions,
cues.zh: 位置嵌入向量，可以把 token 序列拆成一組獨立的時間基底函式，

cues.en: and that allows the model to learn relationships across tokens
cues.zh: 讓模型學習 token 間的關係，

cues.en: in the way that we use relationships across words to indicate meaning and collapse ambiguity.
cues.zh: 就像人類用單字關係表達意義、消除歧義。

cues.en: Nowadays, it is common to train model-specific position embeddings vectors that reflect the sequence characteristics of the texts that the model is trained on.
cues.zh: 現在，常見做法是訓練模型專屬的位置嵌入，反映訓練文字的序列特性。

cues.en: And also a more general point, cosine similarity matrices pack a ton of information into a small amount of space.
cues.zh: 更一般地說，餘弦相似度矩陣，能在很小空間裡，容納大量資訊。

cues.en: They're tricky to interpret, especially when you're first encountering them, but we will continue using these kinds of matrices throughout the course.
cues.zh: 一開始很難解讀，但課程會持續使用這種矩陣。

cues.en: So you'll gain a lot more familiarity with this way of representing network structure and network activity.
cues.zh: 你會越來越熟悉，這種表示網路結構與網路活動的方式。
